info.name: AISafe - Flight Routes (distributed)
info.description:
Tests of the Flight Routes component with 3 replicas (SIDIS Assignment 1).
Prerequisite: from code/, `./scripts/start-replicas.sh flightroutes demo` (or `.\scripts\start-replicas.ps1 -Service flightroutes -Profiles demo`).
Folders 7 and 8 also need Aircraft Management (am1, port 8081) and Airports (ap1, port 8083): `./scripts/start-all.sh 1 demo` plus flightroutes replicas 2 and 3, or `./scripts/start-all.sh 3 demo`.
Use the environment FlightRoutes.postman_environment.json and run the folders in order (folder 0 creates the tokens).
Before folder 6, STOP replica 2 (port 8184). Folders 7 and 8 create their own data with random identifiers, so they can be run again; they still work with replica 2 stopped.

8. Concurrency (run after folder 7)
item.description:
FlightRoute has optimistic locking (@Version) and a write conflict is answered with 409, but the version is NOT part of the API: GET does not return it and PATCH does not accept it (no ETag/If-Match). A client therefore cannot be told that it is updating stale data: sequential updates are last-writer-wins. A 409 only happens when two PATCHes overlap inside the owner replica.
This folder (1) shows the last-writer-wins behaviour, (2) sends 6 PATCHes in parallel through the 3 replicas from a test script and checks that every answer is 200 or 409 and that the final state is one of the values written.
More load: run sub-folder 8.1 many times from two runners at the same time, e.g. two Postman Collection Runner windows with 50 iterations each, or two terminals with
`npx newman run FlightRoutes.postman_collection.json -e <env exported after folders 0, 7 and 8> --folder "8.1 Concurrent update (run with iterations)" -n 50`
(export the environment with `--export-environment` so both runs use the same ccRouteId and token). Every answer must be 200 or 409.

item.name: Setup: route for the concurrency test (reverse of the folder 7 route) → 201
Client B, still holding the old state, updates minCapacity to 120 → 200 (last writer wins: the version is not exposed)

exec: pm.test("status 200: the stale update is not detected (no version in the API)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test("no version field returned to the client", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.not.have.property("version"));

item.name: 6 parallel PATCHes through the 3 replicas → each 200 or 409, final state consistent

exec: body: { mode: "raw", raw: JSON.stringify({ minCapacity: v }) }
pm.test("every answer is 200 or 409 (never 5xx)", () => statuses.forEach(s => pm.expect([200, 409]).to.include(s)));
pm.test("at least one update succeeded", () => pm.expect(statuses).to.include(200));
pm.test("final minCapacity is one of the values written", () => pm.expect(values).to.include(final.json().minCapacity));
